The doc shows a JSONC example ("opencode.jsonc"), but this note only mentions `opencode.json`. Since neither `opencode.json` nor `opencode.jsonc` is auto-created, consider wording this as “`opencode.json`/`opencode.jsonc` is not auto-created” to avoid implying only the `.json` variant is affected.
```suggestion
OpenCode works out of the box without any config file. The `opencode.json`/`opencode.jsonc`
config is **not auto-created** — you only need to create one when you want to customize
```

This hard-codes the state path as `~/.local/state/opencode/kv.json`, but the CLI derives it from XDG state directories (`xdgState` / `XDG_STATE_HOME`). To keep the docs accurate for users with custom XDG paths (and non-Linux defaults), consider referencing `$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode/kv.json` and optionally noting the usual default (`~/.local/state/opencode/kv.json`).
```suggestion
in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode/kv.json` (typically `~/.local/state/opencode/kv.json`) and persist across restarts.
```

`published()` uses `gh release view ...` without scoping to the `repo`/`GH_REPO` value used elsewhere in this script. If `GH_REPO` is set (or the working directory isn't the same repo), this can read the wrong release or fail. Pass `--repo ${repo}` (or `-R ${repo}`) to keep behavior consistent with the other `gh api "/repos/${repo}/..."` calls.
```suggestion
  const body = await $`gh release view ${tag(to)} --repo ${repo} --json body --jq .body`.text().catch(() => "")
```

`sections`/`section()` still include `plugin` and `github` keys, but `commits()` no longer adds `plugin` or `github` to `areas` (plugin is folded into `sdk`, and `github/` is folded into `extensions/vscode`). Dropping the unused keys (and removing them from the `priority` list) will prevent future confusion about which area strings are actually emitted.

`theme_mode` from config is only applied during initial state resolution. The returned `lock` can still be overridden later via `setMode()` / `lock()` / `unlock()` (which call `pin()` / `free()`), so users can bypass a config-forced mode and persist a different mode in KV. If `theme_mode` is intended to *force* the mode, guard `apply`/`pin`/`free` (or the public methods) to no-op when `config.theme_mode` is `light`/`dark`, and consider hiding/disabled theme-mode commands in that case.

`permissions`/`questions` now only aggregate requests from `directChildren()`. This drops requests for the current root session itself (`sync.data.permission[route.sessionID]` / `sync.data.question[route.sessionID]`), which can cause `PermissionPrompt`/`QuestionPrompt` not to render and the main `Prompt` to mount even though the root session has pending permission/question requests. Include the active session’s own requests in these memos (and in the counts used by `shouldRenderSessionPrompt`).

`permissions`/`questions` now aggregate only over `directChildren()`, which excludes the current root session. That means permission/question requests originating from the root session itself won’t be surfaced here, and `shouldRenderSessionPrompt` may incorrectly render the prompt while root-level requests exist. Include the current session in the aggregation (e.g., combine `session()?.id` with direct children) or otherwise ensure root session requests are counted and displayed.

`Prompt` is now conditionally unmounted, but this effect only clears `promptRef` and leaves the local `prompt` variable intact. Many command handlers in this component call `prompt.set(...)` without guarding, which can now throw (or target a stale ref) when the prompt isn’t rendered (subagent view / permission prompt / question prompt). Consider making `prompt` optional and clearing it alongside `promptRef`, and update call sites to use `promptRef.current` (or optional chaining) so commands don’t crash when the prompt is not mounted.

`resolveThemeModeState` treats config `theme_mode: "system"` as a runtime reset (ignores persisted `theme_mode`/`theme_mode_lock`), but it doesn’t clear those persisted KV keys. Since KV is persisted to `Global.Path.state/kv.json`, removing `theme_mode` from config later can unexpectedly re-apply an old lock/mode. Consider clearing `theme_mode` and `theme_mode_lock` in KV when config explicitly requests `system`, so the reset is durable across future config changes.

On the success path (`code === 0`), the script deletes the backup (`.bak`) without verifying that `UPCOMING_CHANGELOG.md` was actually created/updated by the `opencode ... changelog` command. If `opencode` exits 0 but doesn’t write the file for any reason, this can permanently drop the previous changelog. Consider checking that `UPCOMING_CHANGELOG.md` exists (and is non-empty if that’s expected) before removing the backup; otherwise restore from `.bak` and return a non-zero exit code.

Minor wording/grammar: “skim read” is typically hyphenated (“skim-read”) or rephrased (“skim”). Consider adjusting to avoid distracting phrasing in the prompt.
```suggestion
- Focus on writing the least words to get your point across - users will skim the changelog, so we should be precise
```

Minor wording/grammar: “flow on effects” is usually written “flow-on effects” (or “downstream effects”). Consider updating for clarity in the prompt.
```suggestion
**Importantly, the changelog is for users (who are at least slightly technical), they may use the TUI, Desktop, SDK, Plugins and so forth. Be thorough in understanding flow-on effects may not be immediately apparent. e.g. a package upgrade looks internal but may patch a bug. Or a refactor may also stabilise some race condition that fixes bugs for users. The PR title/body + commit message will give you the authors context, usually containing the outcome not just technical detail**
```

PR metadata/title/description indicate this change is only about builtin syntax colors in the TUI theme, but this diff also introduces a new experimental `team` tool (plus config + tests) and registers it in the tool registry. Please either split the `team` tool work into a separate PR or update the PR title/description (and linked issue) to reflect the additional feature, since it materially changes scope and review/rollout risk.

The output/prompt formatting builds XML-like tags with attribute values taken directly from tool inputs (`t.id`, `t.subagent_type`) and derived strings (`state.error`). Because the schema allows arbitrary strings, quotes/newlines can break the markup (and make dependency-result prepending ambiguous). Consider restricting `id`/`subagent_type` to a safe pattern (e.g., `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`) and/or escaping attribute values before embedding them in `<dependency ...>` / `<agent ...>` tags.

`seedAction` treats any non-`undefined` probe result as success, but this code uses `if (!result)` which will incorrectly throw if the probe ever returns a falsy success value (e.g., `false`). Check specifically for `result === undefined` (or restrict the probe type to `Promise<true | undefined>` and keep the check aligned).
```suggestion
  if (result === undefined) throw new Error("Timed out seeding patch")
```

`focus?.hasSelection()` will still attempt to call `hasSelection` whenever `focus` is non-null; if the currently focused renderable is not a text-input-like renderable that implements `hasSelection`, this will throw at runtime. Consider guarding the method call (e.g., optional-chain the method or check `typeof focus.hasSelection === "function"`) before using it, and similarly avoid assuming `sel.selectedRenderables` always exists on the selection object.
```suggestion
    const hasSelection =
      focus && typeof (focus as any).hasSelection === "function"
        ? (focus as any).hasSelection()
        : false
    const selectedRenderables = Array.isArray((sel as any).selectedRenderables)
      ? sel.selectedRenderables
      : []
    if (hasSelection && selectedRenderables.includes(focus)) return
```

The streaming timer interval is started whenever `final()` is false, but messages with `finish: "tool-calls"` / `"unknown"` are intentionally non-final and still get `time.completed` set (e.g. tool execution). In that case this interval will run indefinitely and keep updating `now` even though the elapsed time is already fixed. Consider gating the interval on `props.message.time.completed` (or equivalent streaming state) rather than `final()`, so it stops once the assistant message has a completion timestamp.
```suggestion
    const completed = props.message.time?.completed
    if (final() || completed) return
```

`elapsed()` recomputes by scanning the full `messages()` array to find the parent user message. While streaming, this memo will update every second; with long sessions this becomes a repeated O(n) search per tick. Consider caching the parent user created timestamp (e.g., memoize the parent message lookup once per assistant message, or index messages by id) so timer ticks don’t repeatedly traverse the full message list.

PR description mentions adding git branch display in the sidebar footer, but the current change set shown here only updates per-message timing in `session/index.tsx`. If the sidebar footer work is intended to be part of this PR, it looks like the related file changes may be missing from the branch/commit set (or from the PR).

Suggestion: Consider renaming `next` to `ok` or `done` - the variable holds a boolean result, and `next` suggests it might be "the next value" rather than "did it succeed". This would make the intent clearer at the call site.

`SidebarContent`'s props type still requires `renderPanel`, but the component no longer uses it and `layout.tsx` no longer passes it. This will cause a TypeScript error at the call site; either remove `renderPanel` (and any other now-unused props like `opened`/`aimMove` if applicable) from the prop type, or reintroduce the panel rendering.

The Filter/Sort/View toolbar buttons are rendered as enabled `IconButton`s but have no click handler or disabled state, so they are focusable yet do nothing. If these actions aren't implemented yet, mark them disabled/aria-disabled (or hide them); otherwise wire them to the intended handlers/menus to avoid confusing UX and accessibility issues.
`SidebarContent` still imports `createEffect`/`createMemo` but no longer uses them in this file. Removing unused imports reduces dead code and avoids potential lint/CI failures.

`ProjectSidebarContext` was changed to remove the hover/aim-related fields, but `layout.tsx` still constructs `projectSidebarCtx` with properties like `hoverProject`, `onProjectMouseEnter`, and `onHoverOpenChanged`. With the current exported type, that assignment will fail type-checking; either re-add the removed fields to the context type or update `layout.tsx` to stop passing/using them.
```suggestion
} & Record<string, unknown>
```

The project header row lost the `data-action="project-switch"` / `data-project` attributes and no longer calls `ctx.navigateToProject` on click (it only toggles expansion). This breaks the existing project-switch interaction and the e2e selector that targets `[data-action="project-switch"][data-project=...]` (see `packages/app/e2e/selectors.ts`). Consider restoring those data attributes and providing a click target that navigates to the project while keeping the chevron for expand/collapse.

There are now unused imports in this module (`createEffect` and `useLayout` are imported but not referenced after the rewrite). Cleaning these up improves maintainability and avoids potential lint/CI failures.

`--main-left` switches between `${side()}px` (opened) and `16rem` (closed), while the sidebar nav is fixed `w-64`. If `side()` differs from 256px (e.g., due to persisted `layout.sidebar.width()`), the main content left offset will no longer match the actual sidebar width. It would be safer to compute `--main-left` from the same fixed width (or use `side()` consistently for the nav width as well).

The new project row no longer renders a dedicated menu trigger element with `data-action="project-menu"` / `data-project=...`, but existing e2e flows look for that selector (see `packages/app/e2e/selectors.ts`). If the UI still needs a clickable “more options” affordance (and to keep automation stable), add an explicit menu button inside the row with those data attributes, or update the e2e actions to open the context menu via right-click. ```suggestion as="div" classList={{ "flex items-center gap-2 px-4 py-2 w-full text-left transition-colors": true, "hover:bg-surface-base-hover": true, "bg-surface-base-active": isSelected(), }} > ```

`SessionProcessor.metadata()` performs an async `session.updatePart(...)` based on a snapshot of `ctx.toolcalls[toolCallID]`. Because tools can call `ctx.metadata(...)` without awaiting (e.g. bash streams), this can race with the stream’s own tool state updates (notably `tool-call` setting the real `input`). If the metadata update finishes after a newer tool-call update, `patch()` will write back a stale `input` (often `{}` from the pending state) and/or stale `time`, effectively clobbering the more recent state.

Consider avoiding `updatePart` when the part is still `pending` (only queue into `toolmeta` and apply it during `tool-call`), or serialize/coalesce tool-part writes per `toolCallID` (e.g. a per-tool semaphore) so metadata updates can’t overwrite newer tool state fields like `input`/`time`.
```suggestion
          if (!part || part.state.status !== "running") return
```

The new queued tool metadata behavior (`toolmeta` + applying it in `tool-input-start` / `tool-call`) isn’t covered by a regression test in this PR. It would be good to add a test that calls `metadata()` before the tool transitions to `running`, then emits the `tool-call` event, and asserts the resulting running/error/completed tool part still contains the queued metadata (e.g. `sessionId`) and that `input` is preserved correctly after the transition.

`cleanup()` runs after each assistant message processing attempt (via `Effect.ensuring(cleanup())`), so `MemoryFile.updateMemoryFile(...)` will execute repeatedly during a session rather than “at session end” as described. This can add avoidable IO and churn, and may rewrite MEMORY.md even when no new memories were extracted. Consider deferring the update to a session-idle/finalizer point, or tracking a “dirty” flag in the extractor/store to update only when needed.

MemoryExtractor is initialized inside `process()` for each assistant generation. Since the extractor is a module-level singleton, this design is not safe if multiple sessions/processors run concurrently (state will be overwritten and tool calls from different sessions can interleave). Consider making the extractor state per-session (e.g., Map keyed by sessionID) or instantiating an extractor per `SessionProcessor.create()` handle.

`onUserMessage()` is never called from the session pipeline (no production call sites found), so the “preference” and “decision” patterns won’t be extracted in real sessions. Add a hook where user text parts are ingested (before any system-reminder rewriting) to feed original user messages into the extractor.

PR description mentions “deduplication by topic”, but `save()` always inserts a new row and the schema/migration only adds a non-unique index on `(project_path, topic)`. This will accumulate duplicates across sessions. Consider adding a UNIQUE constraint on `(project_path, topic)` and using an upsert (or explicit delete/update) so each topic stays deduped per project.
```suggestion
        // Ensure deduplication by topic per project by removing any existing entries
        db
          .delete(MemoryTable)
          .where(and(eq(MemoryTable.project_path, input.projectPath), eq(MemoryTable.topic, input.topic)))
          .run()

        db
          .insert(MemoryTable)
          .values({
            id: crypto.randomUUID(),
            project_path: input.projectPath,
            type: input.type,
            topic: input.topic,
            content: input.content,
            session_id: input.sessionId,
            access_count: 0,
          })
          .run()
```

`MemoryFile.updateMemoryFile()` renders each memory as a single markdown bullet (`- ${m.content}`), but extracted `content` can contain newlines (e.g., from captured error output). That will produce malformed/ambiguous markdown where subsequent lines aren’t indented under the bullet. Consider normalizing `m.content` for markdown (indent continuation lines or replace newlines) before writing.

The extractor persists slices of user messages and tool outputs/errors into the DB and writes them to `.opencode/MEMORY.md` without any redaction or secret filtering. This can easily capture credentials, tokens, or proprietary data and then persist it on disk (and potentially into VCS if the directory is committed). Consider adding secret redaction (common token/key patterns), an allowlist of safe sources, and/or defaulting `memory.enabled` to false with explicit opt-in.

The new `memory` table migration does not enforce topic deduplication (no UNIQUE constraint). If topic-level dedupe is required, add a unique index/constraint on `(project_path, topic)` and update the store to upsert accordingly.

DB cleanup in this test uses `db.run(...).run()` inside a `try/catch {}`; if the chained `.run()` is invalid, cleanup is skipped silently. Use `db.run(sql)` (no chaining) and avoid swallowing errors so the test reliably starts from a clean table.

`max_memory_lines` is defined as `z.number().default(200)` without `.int().positive().min(0)` guards. Negative or fractional values would lead to confusing trimming behavior (e.g., `slice(0, -5)` drops lines). Consider validating this as a non-negative integer (similar to other numeric config fields).
```suggestion
          max_memory_lines: z
            .number()
            .int()
            .min(0)
            .default(200)
            .describe("Maximum lines of memory to inject into system prompt"),
```

```suggestion
Suggest the next message the user would naturally type.

The test: Would they think "I was just about to type that"?

Rules:
- Write in the user's voice, not the assistant's ("run the tests", not "Let me run the tests")
- Be specific — "run the tests" beats "continue"
- Match the user's tone and language
- If the conversation is new or vague, steer toward a concrete starter rather than staying silent
- Output NO_SUGGESTION if the task is complete or no natural next step exists

Never suggest:
- Evaluative responses ("looks good", "that worked")
- Questions — predict actions, not curiosity
- New ideas the user didn't ask about
- Multiple asks in one line

Format: 2–12 words for in-flow tasks; one full sentence for cold-start or vague contexts. No quotes, labels, or explanation.
```

Guidance budget is tracked in UTF-8 bytes, but truncation uses `entry.substring(0, remaining)` which is character-count based. This can exceed the byte budget for multibyte characters, can split surrogate pairs, and the appended truncation marker (`\n...(instructions truncated...)`) adds additional bytes beyond the computed `remaining`. Consider performing byte-accurate truncation (e.g., TextEncoder/Buffer slicing) and reserving space for the marker so the returned strings never exceed `budget` bytes.

When only per-line pruning occurs (no line-count/byte-count truncation), `allKept` returns `{ truncated: false }` even though `content` differs from the original text. Several call sites decide whether to use `out.content` based on `out.truncated` (e.g., tool registry wrapper), so long lines may remain unpruned in those paths. Consider making the return shape distinguish between “content modified” vs “full output saved to disk”, or ensure callers always use the returned `content` even when `truncated` is false.

In `prune()`, this uses the static `Provider.getModel(...)` (which spins up its own runtime) instead of the already-injected `provider` service available in this Effect scope. Switching to `yield* provider.getModel(...)` avoids extra runtime construction and keeps dependency handling consistent with the rest of this file.
```suggestion
        let context = 0
        if (lastUser?.model) {
          context = yield* provider
            .getModel(lastUser.model.providerID, lastUser.model.modelID)
            .pipe(
              Effect.map((m) => m.limit.context),
              Effect.catchAll(() => Effect.succeed(0)),
            )
        }
```

New guidance-budget behavior in `InstructionPrompt.system()` isn’t covered by existing instruction tests (which currently focus on `systemPaths()`/`resolve()`). Add tests for: (1) budgeting across multiple instruction sources, (2) truncation marker insertion, and (3) byte-accurate behavior with multibyte UTF-8 content.

Per-line mid-ellipsis pruning (`MAX_LINE_BYTES`/`pruneLine`) is new behavior but isn’t covered by the existing truncation tests. Add cases that verify long single-line output under `maxBytes` gets pruned to `maxLineBytes`, preserves valid Unicode (no broken surrogate pairs), and clarify/lock in whether this should set `truncated` true or false.

Compaction’s new tool-call deduplication and error age-gate purging logic isn’t covered by existing `session.compaction.prune` tests. Add tests that ensure: (1) older duplicates are compacted and only the most recent keeps output, and (2) errored tool inputs older than `ERROR_PURGE_TURNS` have large string fields cleared while preserving the error itself.
